## Summary

Jekyll supports showing all future content but I couldn't find a way to only show a single collection's future content.

The reason this is useful to me is that in general I don't want to display future content but I have a "talks" collection and I would like to show talks I am doing in the future.

-->

+      site = fixture_site
+      collection = Jekyll::Collection.new(site, "methods")
+      collection.metadata["future"] = true

+    end
+
+    should "not be hidden in the future" do
+      refute @publisher.hidden_in_the_future?(@thing)
+    end
+  end

linked_issues.title: Issue with highlighting load tags for Django code
linked_issues.body:
###### I am using Jekyll 3.1.1 on Mac OS X 10.11.2 and I am using Rouge for syntax highlighting. In my markdown file, I am intend to highlight the following code ``` jinja {% load pipeline %} {% block title %}Build with the Github API{% endblock %} {% stylesheet 'yokogao' %}
{% block content %} {% endblock %}
{% block extra_scripts %} {% endblock %} ``` When I run `jekyll serve` it returns the following error: ``` ➜ test-site git:(master) ✗ jekyll serve --profile Configuration file: /Users/raybesiga/Projects/test-site/_config.yml Source: /Users/raybesiga/Projects/test-site Destination: /Users/raybesiga/Projects/test-site/_site Incremental build: disabled. Enable with --incremental Generating... Liquid Exception: Liquid syntax error: Unknown tag 'load' in /Users/raybesiga/Projects/test-site/_posts/2016-02-23-basic-django-app-github-api.markdown jekyll 3.1.1 | Error: Liquid syntax error: Unknown tag 'load' ``` I expected this to work as expected but not sure why it is raising an error. Any advise and help will be highly appreciated

linked_issues.title: Allow configuring 'future' metadata for individual collections
linked_issues.body:
## Summary

Currently, `future` config key is global and affects all collections in the site simultaneously. It would be awesome if users were able to exert finer control on which collections with future-dated documents should be iterable / renderable.

## Motivation

This comment by @pathawks :point_right: https://github.com/jekyll/jekyll/pull/6506#issuecomment-340675231

> I think we might consider making future available as a per-collection option.
Perhaps I don’t want my site built with future blog posts, but do want future events.
I think the current future option was added when posts were the only dated content. That is no longer the case.

## Guide-level explanation

- Ideally, `site.future` would be marked as deprecated with a fallback to automatically setting `collection.metadata["future"]` automatically set to `false (default) or true`. But we could also continue using this key as a global override.
- Usage:
  ```yaml
  future: true # all collections are configured with this global override
               # same behavior as in Jekyll 3.x
  collections:
    posts:
      future: true # renders and writes future-dated posts i.e. {{ site.posts }} will have
                   # future-dated posts and they will get written to `_site` directory.
    members:
      output: true
      future: false # does not render / write future-dated documents i.e. {{ site.members }}
                    # will not show future-dated docs nor will they get written to the `_site`
                    # directory.
    events:
      output: true
      future: "read-only" # future-dated docs can be accessed via {{ site.events }} but
                          # will not be written to the `_site` directory.
  ```
- Basically, the metadata key expects three values: **`true`**, **`false`** or **`read-only`**


## Drawbacks

- Added complexity in sites with numerous collections

<!--
## Unresolved Questions
  What related issues do you consider out of scope for this feature that could be
  addressed in the future independently of the solution that comes out of this
  feature?
